conventions.convention: Rates and entropies use natural logarithms and are measured in nats per channel use; achievable rates use a liminf of normalized log code size.
Quantum codes have isometric encoders and CPTP decoders; reliability means that the squared overlap with the maximally entangled target tends to one.
Private codes have uniform messages, possibly mixed input states, average decoding error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero.
Entanglement-assisted codes allow arbitrary finite shared states independent of the message, message-dependent CPTP encoders, and unrestricted shared-state dimension and consumption.
A complement is associated with a chosen finite Stinespring dilation; coherent information is S(B)−S(BR), independent of the purification.
Degradability means Nᶜ=D∘N, while antidegradability means N=A∘Nᶜ, using the fixed complementary dilation.
The erasure channel acts on the full operator space, has input dimension d≥1, erasure probability ε∈[0,1], and an orthogonal one-dimensional output flag.
Conditional spectral-projector rank and eigenvalue bounds hold for every word, including zero-probability words; high acceptance is asserted only after averaging.

load_bearing.statement: For finite bipartite states and local quantum channels Φ and Ψ, I(A′:B′) under (Φ⊗Ψ)(ρ) is at most I(A:B) under ρ.
For states ρᵢ and finite probabilities pᵢ, with ρ̄=Σᵢpᵢρᵢ, 0≤S(ρ̄)−ΣᵢpᵢS(ρᵢ)≤H(p).

Every fixed finite ensemble and fixed η>0 admit global and word-dependent spectral projectors with the stated exponential rank/eigenvalue bounds and exponentially small averaged failure probabilities.

For D≥2, 1≤K≤D, positive ω with trace at most one, r=rank(ω_E), and δ>0, a specified finite isometry ensemble has expected decoupling trace norm at most √(2Kr tr(ω²))+δ and simultaneously contracts every Hermitian compression in expectation by at most 1+δ.

For states on dimension d and t=½‖ρ−σ‖₁, |S(ρ)−S(σ)|≤t ln d+g(t). A uniform ensemble with mean distance a from a fixed state has Holevo information at most 2a ln d+2g(a), where g(t)=(1+t)ln(1+t)−t ln t and g(0)=0.

The exact orthogonal flat spectral-type decomposition of ρ⊗n has H(T)≤d ln(n+1); average type coherent information is at least nI_c(ρ,N)−H(T), and average type S+I_c is at least n[S(ρ)+I_c(ρ,N)]−2H(T). Each bound is attained or exceeded by some type.

For flat input τ, every 0<R<I_c(τ,N) is achievable by isometric subspace entanglement transmission with squared target overlap tending to one; the result also holds for flat states on input subspaces.

For any finite input ensemble and fixed complement, every 0<R<χ_B−χ_E admits uniform mixed-input codes with rate tending to R, average error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero.
For a flat state τ on a nonzero input subspace, every 0≤R<S(τ)+I_c(τ,N) is achievable using shared maximally entangled states, finite Weyl operations, and collective output/reference POVMs.
Every finite extension ω_ZA of ρ_A is obtained from a purification ψ_RA, with R a copy of A, by a CPTP map Λ:R→Z acting on its reference.
Coherent information of a finite degradable channel is concave and nonnegative; for two degradable channels it is subadditive on arbitrary joint inputs, and its optimized value is additive.
For d≥1 and ε∈[0,1], Q(E_d,ε)=P(E_d,ε)=max{1−2ε,0} ln d and C_E(E_d,ε)=2(1−ε) ln d.

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 defines K_0=√α J_E J_B* and then defines K_j=√(1−α)|e_E⟩⟨u_j| for j<d, which includes j=0. Step 3.1 repeats the collision with L_0 and L_j for j<d. The intended Kraus lists and normalization calculations are clear, but the same operator label receives two different definitions.

Fact F5 contains the literal overescaped formula $(\\exp)'=\\exp$. The doubled backslashes introduce TeX line-break commands instead of the intended exponential commands; the cited supplier states the ordinary derivative identity correctly.

Fact F3 writes the Cauchy–Schwarz formula with literal doubled backslashes before langle, rangle, leq, lVert, and rVert. These are overescaped mathematical commands in the Markdown carrier, although the underlying inequality and its uses are correct.

Step 2.1 says 'The lower mixture bound [F1] gives' Σ_t p_t S(B_t)≥S(B̄)−H(T), and 'its upper bound gives' Σ_t p_t S(E_t)≤S(Ē). The displayed inequalities are correct, but the first uses the upper entropy-excess bound and the second uses the lower bound; the verbal labels are reversed.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and its Schumacher, HSW, gentle-measurement, and fixed-dimensional continuity interfaces against their actual uses. The source page supplies finite-dimensional coding results in nats, with squared entanglement fidelity for compression and deterministic finite-alphabet cq codes with average error for HSW. The consumer uses HSW on a fixed finite Weyl alphabet for each fixed block channel; it does not extend HSW to an unrestricted quantum-input single-letter formula. Growing-dimension continuity needed for quantum converses and strong secrecy is supplied separately within batch 24. The prerequisite page makes no reverse capacity claim requiring correction.
